content:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-31
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Aaron Patel (Redwood SE), Leah Morris (Redwood CSM); Sofia Alvarez (Orchid Channel Lead), Tom Reed (Orchid VP Sales), Nina Park (Orchid Solution Architect)
Recording link: (recording omitted)
Shared artifacts: joint pipeline spreadsheet (link: https://tiny.redwood/orchid-pipeline), security one-pager (link: https://tiny.redwood/sec-orchid), demo deck (link: https://tiny.redwood/demo-orchid)

Summary:
Quick partner co-sell review across top 6 deals. Focus on Meridian Systems (mid-funnel, technical eval next week), Solstice Retail (proof-of-concept requested — legal review around data residency), and NovaHealth (exec-level procurement timeline). Discussed integration constraints (VPC, K M S notes), routing fallbacks, and a lightweight benchmark Redwood SE can run. Agreed next steps: update pipeline spreadsheet, run partner-led demo, share SOW/pricing ranges, and schedule exec alignment.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy new year eve, uh, really appreciate you squeezing this in, we'll keep to 45 minutes ish and leave time for q and a.
[00:12] Sofia: thanks Maya, likewise, appreciate it. we have Tom and Nina on from business and technical side.
[00:18] Tom: hi all.
[00:20] Nina: hi, thanks.
[00:25] Maya: quick agenda — 1) pipeline review top deals, 2) blockers and security/compliance items, 3) alignment on who owns demos and next steps. Aaron from our SE team will jump in on Meridian and the bench plan.
[00:36] Aaron: hey folks, real quick — i'll go through a proposed checklist we can run partner-side; it's lightweight: sample prompt set, token cost estimate, latency baseline on your infra or our hosted, and a KV cache smoke test; i realize i said KV cash last time in the doc so forgive the typo.
[00:52] Sofia: ok good, that sounds reasonable. for Meridian they said they care a lot about latency under 200ms for short responses and that cost must be 60% below our current vendor.
[01:03] Tom: yeah, latency and price, and also data residency — NovaHealth is insisting on EU-only processing and audit logs.
[01:11] Leah: for NovaHealth we flagged private deployment as an option, we can do VPC or on-prem depending on compliance, S O C 2 controls are in place—we have a security one-pager i'll share.
[01:24] Nina: about V P C — can you clarify egress controls and K M S integration? our infra team is picky.
[01:30] Aaron: absolutely. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and H S M integrations, per-tenant key wraps; egress rules can be locked down to specific subnets. i'll add a short diagram to the sheet.
[01:45] Sofia: great. in the pipeline doc Meridian is currently marked as committed for a pilot but needs a technical check next week — can redwood run the partner-led demo and bench?
[01:55] Maya: yes that's fine; we suggest a partner-led demo with an SE co-presenting. Aaron, you'd be the handoff for the technical breakup?
[02:03] Aaron: yep. i'll prep a 30-minute partner-led session with a 15-minute bench run. checklist i'll use: sample prompts, tokenization estimates, expected throughput for 8k context and 2k typical, and a KV cache prefix test.
[02:18] Tom: 8k context — Meridian's use is mostly short chat completions but they want longer context for customer history occasionally. they also asked about quantized model options to save cost.
[02:29] Aaron: we can run quantized variants; recommend running both fp16 and 8-bit qlv tests to see quality delta. i'll include those notes.
[02:38] Sofia: question — do you have any existing customers in retail who required EU-only processing? Solstice Retail might push back.
[02:46] Leah: yes we have a few; most moved to Redwood Private with a VPC and dedicated capacity, we can share redacted audit logs. i'll attach case references.
[02:56] Nina: are your audit logs immutable? our compliance team asks about retention and tamper evidence.
[03:03] Aaron: logs are append-only in our control plane, and we support forwarding to customer SIEMs. tamper evidence is through signed immutable buckets when needed. i'll follow up with the security doc link.
[03:15] Tom: competition — Meridian shortlisted AWS Bedrock and Vertex AI, Solstice is also talking to Anthropic for chat-first use cases. how do we position Redwood?
[03:26] Maya: we emphasize serving economics and predictable latency — e.g., dedicated pools, KV cache features, and the ability to pin model variants for rollouts. also the unified interface across hosted/dedicated/private is a differentiator.
[03:40] Sofia: price will be sensitive — can you share ballpark ranges and an S O W for pilot costs?
[03:46] Maya: yes — we'll send a pilot SOW template and ranges. note that Dedicated commitment discounts vary; i'll include both hosted and dedicated ranges in the doc.
[03:56] Nina: technical: for the pilot, do you support function calling and tool integrations? our backend will need to call internal APIs.
[04:03] Aaron: yes, function/tool calling is supported; the runtime also supports streaming responses and structured output. if they need custom tools we can discuss secure connectors.
[04:13] Sofia: ok can we go through the top three deals quickly? Meridian, Solstice, NovaHealth.
[04:18] Maya: Meridian — status: mid-funnel, partner-led demo next Wed, technical eval same week. owner: Sofia/Tom for partner, Maya for Redwood. ask: bench and demo.
[04:29] Maya: Solstice Retail — status: POC requested, security/legal gating (data residency). owner: Nina for technical due diligence, Leah supporting.
[04:37] Maya: NovaHealth — status: exec procurement, procurement timeline Jan 15, needs SOC2 attestation and HIPAA notes. owner: Leah to provide artifacts.
[04:47] Tom: for NovaHealth, is HIPAA supported?
[04:50] Leah: we have customers in regulated spaces; we offer Private deployments and BAA conversations. i'll bring legal into the thread.
[04:58] Nina: about benchmarks — can you run an end-to-end with our sample data? including hitting our internal APIs for tool calls?
[05:05] Aaron: yes, partner-driven bench can include calling customer APIs; we'll need sandbox creds or a stub environment. recommend a simple stub.
[05:15] Sofia: timeline question — if Meridian likes the pilot, what's typical time to production?
[05:20] Maya: typical is 6-10 weeks from pilot to prod for mid-market with private deployment; shorter if they stay hosted. we'll map that in the pipeline sheet as a best-case/worst-case.
[05:34] Tom: procurement — any gotchas around contract length for Dedicated?
[05:38] Maya: Dedicated has reserved capacity commits, often 12 months; we can do trial bursts and convert credits. we'll note options in SOW.
[05:47] Nina: one more question — do you support role-based access controls and S S O integration?
[05:51] Leah: yes, SAML S S O and granular RBAC is supported; we also provide audit trails for token usage.
[05:59] Sofia: ok great. action items?
[06:02] Maya: i'll update the joint pipeline sheet right after this call with the new owners and dates. i'll also send the pilot SOW and pricing ranges.
[06:08] Aaron: i'll prepare the bench checklist and sample prompts plus quantization plan; will share by Monday.
[06:14] Nina: i'll send integration questions and a stub env for Meridian by Friday.
[06:18] Leah: i'll pull SOC2 and HIPAA artifact list and share the security one-pager.
[06:24] Tom: thanks everyone.
[06:26] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up in the shared spreadsheet and schedule the exec alignment. enjoy the rest of your day.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hear (K V cash vs KV cache) and some shorthand acronyms expanded in notes. Speakers labelled where possible but upload had slight speaker overlap in a few spots.

End of transcript.
